editorial:
Imagine you are in England right after World War II, where everything feels grey and lonely. You follow a woman who makes a living debunking fake ghosts. She gets called to a creepy boys boarding school where people claim to see a dead student. It feels like a classic mystery from the start, with a cool 1940s look and a heavy sense of dread. You will feel like you are walking through those cold, empty hallways right along with her as she tries to prove that the ghosts are just tricks of the mind.

The acting is top-notch and keeps you glued to the screen, even though the story moves a bit slow at times. The big twist at the end is what really makes the whole trip worth it. If you love a good puzzle, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick night in, or if you want the best picture quality, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go. It looks great in high definition, which makes the dark corners of the school feel even more real.
endingExplained: You find out that the main character is actually a ghost herself. She died in a car crash before the movie started, but she did not realize it. She was not solving a mystery for the living; she was seeing her own past. The ghost she was chasing was actually a memory. Once she accepts that she is dead, she finally finds peace and moves on to the afterlife.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves ghost stories with a big twist.
